svg.title: Base Case: $705,000 Revenue to $267,900 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-owner-profit-bridge; chart type: waterfall; title: Base Case: $705,000 Revenue to $267,900 Owner Profit; subtitle: Six bars reconcile annual service revenue, four cost pools, and the ending total.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Canonical Formula v2.0 totals are fixed; the four expense pools are an illustrative allocation of $437,100. The first and last bars are totals; the four interior values are signed changes. Revenue excludes client trust balances, settlements, and pass-through amounts for which the MSO is an agent.; caption: $705,000 - $180,000 - $144,000 - $66,000 - $47,100 = $267,900; $267,900 / $705,000 = 38.0%. Conservative: $160,000 revenue, $118,400 costs, $41,600 profit at 26%. Scaled: $1,250,000 revenue, $625,000 costs, $625,000 profit at 50%.; stages: label: Recognized service revenue; value: $705,000 annual contracted administrative service revenue; numeric value: 705000.0; detail: Equivalent to twelve $58,750 monthly service invoices earned through contracted delivery. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to reimbursed media and retrieval charges; no separate retained-share factor is supplied or invented for this canonical revenue total.; label: Acquisition delivery expense; value: Subtract $180,000 for owned campaign delivery costs; numeric value: -180000.0; detail: Allocate $15,000 monthly to media and attributable campaign production where the MSO bears those costs. Audit source quality and vendor credits. Direct law-firm media spend is outside this MSO expense pool.; label: Pod delivery labor; value: Subtract $144,000 for contracted and employed delivery capacity; numeric value: -144000.0; detail: Illustrative annual pool: $60,000 employed operations seat, $30,000 intake contractor, $30,000 record contractor, and $24,000 chronology contractor. Treat amounts as loaded planning allowances; contractor seats represent scheduled capacity, not three additional full-time employees.; label: Record and triage outlays; value: Subtract $66,000 for retrieval and evidence-processing expenses; numeric value: -66000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $36,000 to provider and pharmacy retrieval, $18,000 to secure parsing and processing, and $12,000 to external exception work. Keep pod labor outside this pool to prevent double counting.; label: Core overhead expense; value: Subtract $47,100 for recurring non-delivery operating support; numeric value: -47100.0; detail: Budget $3,925 monthly for secure systems, insurance, bookkeeping, contract maintenance, and general administration. The supplied $2,500-$14,000 monthly opex range is treated here as core recurring overhead, not total modeled costs of $36,425 monthly.; label: Annual owner profit; value: $267,900 ending profit equals a 38.0% net margin; numeric value: 267900.0; detail: This is the canonical modeled owner-profit measure after the four expense pools, not a settlement share. Tax treatment, owner distributions, and cash timing remain separate schedules; do not count collections again after recognizing earned service revenue.

text.title: Base Case: $705,000 Revenue to $267,900 Owner Profit
text.tspan: Base Case: $705,000 Revenue to $267,900 Owner Profit

circle.title: label: Recognized service revenue; value: $705,000 annual contracted administrative service revenue; numeric value: 705000.0; detail: Equivalent to twelve $58,750 monthly service invoices earned through contracted delivery. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to reimbursed media and retrieval charges; no separate retained-share factor is supplied or invented for this canonical revenue total.

label: Acquisition delivery expense; value: Subtract $180,000 for owned campaign delivery costs; numeric value: -180000.0; detail: Allocate $15,000 monthly to media and attributable campaign production where the MSO bears those costs. Audit source quality and vendor credits. Direct law-firm media spend is outside this MSO expense pool.

label: Pod delivery labor; value: Subtract $144,000 for contracted and employed delivery capacity; numeric value: -144000.0; detail: Illustrative annual pool: $60,000 employed operations seat, $30,000 intake contractor, $30,000 record contractor, and $24,000 chronology contractor. Treat amounts as loaded planning allowances; contractor seats represent scheduled capacity, not three additional full-time employees.

label: Record and triage outlays; value: Subtract $66,000 for retrieval and evidence-processing expenses; numeric value: -66000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $36,000 to provider and pharmacy retrieval, $18,000 to secure parsing and processing, and $12,000 to external exception work. Keep pod labor outside this pool to prevent double counting.

label: Core overhead expense; value: Subtract $47,100 for recurring non-delivery operating support; numeric value: -47100.0; detail: Budget $3,925 monthly for secure systems, insurance, bookkeeping, contract maintenance, and general administration. The supplied $2,500-$14,000 monthly opex range is treated here as core recurring overhead, not total modeled costs of $36,425 monthly.

label: Annual owner profit; value: $267,900 ending profit equals a 38.0% net margin; numeric value: 267900.0; detail: This is the canonical modeled owner-profit measure after the four expense pools, not a settlement share. Tax treatment, owner distributions, and cash timing remain separate schedules; do not count collections again after recognizing earned service revenue.
